NoteTexAccessor::envs¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::envs() const

Extract Complete Environment Regions¶

envs() extracts complete \begin{name}...\end{name} regions from every Text cell. Each token retains the opener, body, and closer. This makes the result suitable for relocating or separately processing authored blocks without reconstructing delimiters or losing the environment name.

Unlike env_names(), this method requires a matching closer with the same name. An unmatched opener or closer contributes no token. Starred environment names are matched literally, so \begin{figure*} closes only at \end{figure*}. Results retain source order and duplicates.

The return type is a TokenBatch, not a shape-preserving Note. tokens() is a flat Text Note containing every extracted region; offsets() maps each logical receiver cell to its half-open token range. This representation handles a different number of environments per cell without nested host containers.

envs() performs extraction only. It does not render content, remove the regions from the receiver, or validate commands inside a body. Use remove_environment(name) for removal and extract_environment(name) when a known environment kind should be selected directly. Undefined input returns an undefined token Note with offsets [0]; non-text input is rejected.

Example 1: Return Whole Regions¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\begin{figure}A\end{figure} \begin{align*}x&=1\end{align*})",
    R"(\begin{table}B\end{table})", "no environment"});
const auto blocks = source.tex().envs();

std::cout << blocks.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{figure}A\\end{figure}", "\\begin{align*}x&=1\\end{align*}", "\\begin{table}B\\end{table}"]

Example 2: Map Regions Back To Cells¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = blocks.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Example 3: Incomplete Regions Are Not Fabricated¶

const auto partial = pluss::make_note(
    {R"(\begin{proof}unfinished)", R"(\end{proof})"})
    .tex().envs();
std::cout << partial.tokens() << '\n';
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (const auto value : partial.offsets().integers())
  std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets=[0, 0, 0]

Example 4: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().envs();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().envs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "environments Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
environments Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • extract_environment: extract only one requested environment kind.

  • remove_environment: remove one requested environment kind.
